match.reason: None of the bank points teaches how to evaluate a program against its goals, who it reached, whether it is sustainable and its SDG links; epidemiology only touches judging a program through disease rates, which is narrower.

draft.title: Evaluating a health program
card: Evaluation checks how well a program worked. It uses evidence, such as data collected before and after the program.
did the program reach what it set out to do? A program that aimed to immunise 80% of children is judged against that target.
who did it help? A program may help many people but miss the groups with the greatest need, such as people in remote villages.
will the benefits last once funding or outside staff leave? A program can also be linked to an SDG, such as Goal 3, good health and wellbeing.
draft.remember: Judge a program by its goals, who it reached, whether it lasts and its SDG links.

a.q: A program set out to vaccinate 80% of children in a district. After two years, 55% were vaccinated. Which part of evaluation does this result mainly address?
opts: Whether the program reached its goals
Whether the program links to an SDG
Whether the program reached the neediest groups
a.why: The result is compared with the 80% target, so it shows whether the goal was reached. It says nothing about who was missed or whether benefits last after support ends.
a.clue: Compare the result with the target that was set.

b.q: A clean water program in a region of Kenya built wells that served many families. Two years later, most wells are broken and nobody locally can fix them. Which is the best evaluation?
opts: It helped many people, but its benefits did not last
It failed on reach, because few families used the wells
It met its goals, so its benefits are sure to last
It will last, because many families were served
b.why: Many families were helped, but the broken wells and lack of local repair skills show the benefits did not last. Serving many people is not the same as lasting, which is the tempting mistake.
b.clue: Separate how many people were helped from whether the benefits last.

a.best: Whether the program reached its goals

b.best: It helped many people, but its benefits did not last
